- Overestimate prices when sentiment is high (especially >0.7) — reduce forecast by 2–5% for high sentiment periods.
- Underestimate prices when sentiment is low (especially <0.3) — increase forecast by 3–7% for low sentiment periods.
- Overshoot after sharp price spikes — cap forecast at 10–15% below peak if sentiment drops sharply post-spike.
- Mean-reversion bias: if 3–5 consecutive days show downward trend, reduce forecast by 1–3% per day until trend reverses.
- Horizon-specific: 30-day forecasts tend to overestimate early in the cycle (first 5–7 days) — adjust down 1–3% for first 7 days if sentiment is neutral or rising.
- Lagged sentiment effect: if sentiment drops 2+ days before forecast horizon, reduce forecast by 2–4% to account for delayed market reaction.
